leads.title: Close the historical CSR balance loop
leads.question: Was the March 2019 pool balance later returned to contributing oil PSUs or used under documented approvals?
neededEvidence: IOCL pool ledger and bank reconciliation from 31 March 2019 through closure.
NOC-wise return instructions, receipt acknowledgments and subsequent programme utilization certificates.
Separate old-BPL and PMUY allocation lines; preserve interest and timing adjustments.
disconfirmingEvidence: Audited return receipts and approved later use fully reconcile the₹261.85 crore opening balance.
leads.feasibility: High for published annual-report/action-taken searches; remaining ledger access may require lawful RTI or voluntary disclosure.

leads.title: Join supplier compensation to household benefit
leads.question: Do recorded LPG under-recoveries, compensation releases and targeted household credits reconcile across the same periods?
neededEvidence: MoPNG allocation formula and twelve-tranche release ledger.
Company-specific audited LPG under-recovery and compensation recognition notes.
Budget actuals and aggregated bank-credit totals for targeted PMUY subsidy.
Import-price, exchange-rate, freight and inventory-cost bridge; do not substitute crude-oil discounts for LPG cost.
disconfirmingEvidence: Company accounts, treasury releases and consumer-credit aggregates reconcile after accrual/cash timing and eligibility differences.
leads.feasibility: High for listed-company reports and fiscal accounts; medium for detailed allocation and transfer ledgers.

leads.title: Test the complete-year cooking-fuel gap
leads.question: Which affordability, supply or payment factors explain lower PMUY refill use in each state?
neededEvidence: Full-year district cohort counts, refill distributions and entry/exit dates.
Representative household fuel-stacking, household-size and alternative-fuel survey.
District delivery distance, subsidy latency and consumer net-price data.
Compare matched cohorts; predefine covariates and report missingness before estimating effects.
disconfirmingEvidence: Differences disappear after household need and alternative clean-fuel use are measured.
High verified clean-fuel use despite low connection-specific LPG purchases.
leads.feasibility: High for aggregate administrative and survey data; causal effects require a defensible design, not cross-state rank correlation.

leads.title: Separate duplicate removal from wrongful exclusion
leads.question: Does termination reduce duplicate subsidies without excluding eligible households facing non-use or authentication barriers?
neededEvidence: Terminations by mutually exclusive reason and state, with denominators.
Appeal/reinstatement rates and resolution times; no personal identifiers.
Compare pre/post-termination delivery and subsidy histories in an anonymized authorized audit.
disconfirmingEvidence: Independent eligibility review shows terminations correctly classified and eligible appellants promptly restored.
leads.feasibility: Medium: published aggregate replies obtainable; individual-level audit requires lawful authorization.

leads.title: Build the missing coal-auction comparison group
leads.question: Does related-entry participation predict reduced effective bidding after mine attributes and 2015 eligibility rules are held constant?
neededEvidence: All 38 offered mines, qualification outcomes, and complete stage-II action logs for the same two 2015 tranches.
Ownership/SEUP relationships frozen at each auction date; no use of later acquisitions.
Geology, reserves, clearances, infrastructure, reserve price and power/non-regulated category.
Independent bidder actions and final price outcomes; pre-register a matching or sensitivity plan before inspecting outcomes.
disconfirmingEvidence: Matched independent-bidder activity and prices do not differ materially.
Contemporaneous documents explain nonparticipation or show competitive independent bids.
leads.feasibility: Medium: audit subset recovered; complete historic logs may require archived notices or lawful disclosure.

leads.title: Trace coal savings into actual electricity tariffs
leads.question: Were benefits from Sarisatolli coal diverted to other plants credited to consumers through tariff orders and true-ups?
neededEvidence: Plant identities and month-wise diversion quantities after August 2015.
Delivered fuel-cost allocation and regulator-approved tariff/true-up orders.
Dates when each regulator received and acted on diversion notifications.
disconfirmingEvidence: Audited cost allocation and regulator true-ups demonstrate full consumer pass-through with valid timing.
leads.feasibility: Medium: public tariff orders can identify plants and cost treatment; complete fuel ledgers may remain unavailable.

leads.title: Join public works only at verified payer and award IDs
leads.question: Can the existing works cohorts link a dated legal payer to an award without mixing subsidiaries, bid stages or programmes?
neededEvidence: Use existing public-works source register and full bidder cohort, not selected critical cases.
Acquire exact legal-entity identifiers, dated ownership and matched award/tender IDs before any political-finance join.
Publish rejected joins and missing denominators; collateral evidence needed for any improper-benefit claim.
disconfirmingEvidence: Same-name firms are distinct, dates are incompatible, or ordinary award criteria explain the association.
leads.feasibility: Medium; existing corpus already contains Bharatmala and public-works analysis. No new works corruption finding is made in this batch.

leads.title: Follow the same donor across distinct programmes
leads.question: Did public oil-company CSR portfolios change across LPG access, PM CARES and other health/community programmes, after total obligations and emergency needs are accounted for?
neededEvidence: All project-level annual CSR schedules for the same legal companies, with total obligations and carry-forwards.
Board approvals, cancellations, recipient acknowledgments and completion outcomes, separated by fiscal year.
Counterfactual community-project budget and demand evidence before alleging crowding out.
disconfirmingEvidence: Total CSR resources expanded, existing projects remained funded and independently verified emergency needs justified the changes.
PMUY pool refunds and later PM CARES payments reconcile as separate funds and dates.
leads.feasibility: High for public company CSR schedules; medium for complete recipient-level outcome and cash reconciliation.

findings.title: Historical CSR arithmetic closes exactly
findings.summary: ₹548.54 crore contributed minus₹226.69 crore PMUYuse minus₹60 crore prior-BPL allocation equals₹261.85 crore idle atMarch 2019. The remaining question is later disposition, not an unexplained arithmetic gap.

findings.title: A real distributional gap needs a causal explanation
findings.summary: FY 2024–25 PMUY refill averages are below non-PMUY averages in all 36 State/UT rows; national 4.47 vs 6.64. Income and household differences prevent a causal fraud inference.

findings.title: Audit subset preserves both concern and counterevidence
findings.summary: All 11 source bid-action totals reconcile:60 qualified entries,39 independent entries reported byCAG,12 zero-action entries and 2,938 bid actions. No all-auction control estimate; CCI 2025 closure remains attached.
